children: Mitsui Chemicals Inc. sees business opportunities in plastic recycling, as the Middle East conflict may accelerate the practice, according to Satoshi Ichimura, president and CEO of the Japanese chemical manufacturer.
"Japanese companies excel in such activities, so new business opportunities may arise," Ichimura said during an interview with The Yomiuri Shimbun.
The following is excerpted from the interview.
The Yomiuri Shimbun: Japan's petrochemical sector is undergoing restructuring. What is the significance of the move?

Satoshi Ichimura: China has adopted a national policy to produce petrochemicals domestically, leading to the construction of tremendous production facilities. As a result, petrochemical products are now overflowing not only in Asia but also in the United States and Europe.

This trend is particularly notable in commodity products, raising serious concerns within (our domestic) industry. Consequently, Japanese chemical manufacturers have teamed up to devise a plan to shut down four of the 12 ethylene plants in Japan.

The plan aims not only to balance supply and demand. Since each company has products it excels in, streamlining the production of commodity products will enhance Japan's overall competitiveness. It also allows companies to cooperate in reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
Yomiuri: Is the Middle East conflict likely to alter the industry's trajectory?
Ichimura: Moves to reduce plastic usage through recycling may accelerate. I believe the crisis has raised public awareness about conserving petrochemical products.

For example, the plastic used in IV bags is made up of multiple layers to prevent air from getting in. If the number of layers could be reduced from five to two while maintaining functionality, recycling would become easier. Japanese companies excel in such activities, so new business opportunities may arise.
Yomiuri: In August, Mitsui Chemicals acquired Ultradent Products Inc., a major U.S. dental materials manufacturer. Could you elaborate on that?

Ichimura: Ultradent Products directly manufactures syringes and other instruments used in dental treatment, allowing it to differentiate its products and be competitive. At the same time, we can provide (Ultradent Products) a variety of materials to meet its needs.

Synergies created by acquisitions like the latest case will be crucial for the future of the fine chemicals business. We must continue to explore fields where we can apply our technologies in chemicals, even in niche areas.
